assessment: A claim this lane posted an hour ago is too strong, and this build is what measured it. c-0024.1 and e-000231 said harvest_intraday's three false misses were owed by exactly the three runs that harvested zero rows, one for one. The ninth build has FIVE zero-yield runs in its window and publishes only TWO misses, so the identity is false. The direction survives and is now measured precisely: every published miss is still a cell VACATED by a zero-yield run, because those runs finish 37-38 s past their slot while the cell edges sit 72-79 s past it, so each bins backward into its predecessor's cell and leaves its own empty. What the previous reading missed is that a vacancy only becomes a published miss if the FOLLOWING run also falls short of the edge and backfills it. That is the whole of the 3 -> 2 change: the anchor advanced 7 seconds (72 s past the slot at the 14:01:12 build, 79 s at 15:01:19) and pulled the 11:31:19 run - whose own offset is 79 s, landing EXACTLY on the edge - out of its own cell and into the vacancy left by 12:00:38, converting a red cell to green with not one row of run history changed. Both strips reproduce cell by cell from emit_build_status.py's own windows() and beats_for(), re-read from source this fire; the ninth matches all 24 cells exactly. So the measured sensitivity of this board's only trustworthiness signal is SEVEN SECONDS OF BUILD CLOCK PER PUBLISHED MISS, which is a sharper statement of the defect than the yield coupling was, and it still does not widen the ask: clause (a), flooring the cell grid to the schedule, removes the anchor dependence and the run-duration dependence together. Nothing else moved. Trunk is 1a05afa for 21.6 days and the executor leg is dead behind it, so dispatch was held for a sixteenth fire on re-measured evidence. One number improved on its own: intraday's over-count cleared to 13/13 and its yield is non-zero for a third consecutive build at 15,785 rows.

items.title: Correcting c-0024.1: the false misses are NOT one-for-one with the zero-yield runs - five vacancies produced two misses, and the strip's sensitivity is seven seconds of build clock per red cell
items.why: Because c-0024.1 and e-000231 are an hour old, are on your board, and state an identity that this build refutes - and the refutation makes the defect easier to act on, not harder. The corrected mechanism: cells in windows() are anchored on generated_at, so this build's edges sit 79 s past each half hour (72 s at the previous build). The five zero-yield runs today finish 37-38 s past their slots and therefore bin BACKWARD into their predecessors' cells, vacating their own; the eight productive runs finish 72-91 s past theirs and sit either side of the edge depending on the second. A vacancy publishes 'miss' only if the next run does not also fall short and backfill it. At 72 s three vacancies went unbackfilled (3 misses); at 79 s the 11:31:19 run - offset exactly 79 s, ON the edge - was pulled back into the 12:00 vacancy and one red cell became green. Same 13 runs, same log, two verdicts one hour apart. This is the same single defect you are already holding, stated at its true sensitivity.
